articleTitle: A Rigorous Numerical Comparison for Parameter Extraction Using Classical and Kullback-Leibler Formulations Illustrated with Full-Wave EM and Equivalent Circuit Models for Microstrip Filters
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Numerical circuit parameter extraction (PE) is a key sub-process of space mapping (SM), which is used to efficiently optimize full-wave EM responses of microwave structures exploiting faster but inaccurate physics-based auxiliary models. Any improvement in PE has a positive impact on SM design optimization. In this paper, we apply for the first time a PE formulation based on the Kullback-Leibler distance to microstrip filters using their full-wave EM responses as targets. We perform a rigorous numerical comparison of PE based on the K-L formulation against PE using classical norms. Our results confirm a better PE performance using the Kullback-Leibler formulation than those obtained with traditional PE formulations.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Post-Silicon Validation: Tackling Signal Integrity Issues in High-Speed Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Semiconductor technology advances, coupled with the demand for higher data rates and bandwidth, has led to significant signal integrity issues such as attenuation, crosstalk, jitter, noise, EM susceptibility, etc. Traditional post-silicon validation methods for high-performance computer platforms, which rely heavily on manual inspection and rule-based heuristics, are increasingly inadequate for addressing these complexities. In this paper, we review and highlight the application of artificial intelligence (AI) approaches and machine learning (ML) techniques to automate post-silicon validation and enhance the detection and diagnosis of signal integrity issues in high-speed computer interfaces. Through a series of case studies, we demonstrate the efficacy of various AI techniques, including artificial neural networks (ANNs), surrogate modeling, and unsupervised learning, in optimizing settings and improving the efficiency of post-silicon validation. These techniques significantly reduce the number of required measurements, enhance accuracy, and provide scalable and flexible solutions for modern post-silicon physical layer validation and tuning processes.

articleTitle: PCI Express Gen6 FIR Filter Optimization by Space Mapping for Post-Silicon Validation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: The evolution of PCI Express technology to Gen6, and the forthcoming Gen7, has markedly increased data transfer speeds, presenting new challenges for signal integrity. To tackle these challenges, advanced design strategies, such as enhanced equalization (EQ) techniques, are necessary. Traditional EQ methods typically involve extensive laboratory measurements, rendering the EQ process highly time intensive. In this paper, we introduce an optimization methodology for the PCIe Gen6 transmitter (Tx) equalizer utilizing the Aggressive Space Mapping (ASM) algorithm. Our ASM approach employs a computationally efficient surrogate as coarse model to estimate eye diagram margins. An implicit mapping between the coarse and fine model equalizer settings is established, leading to an efficient optimization for the EQ tuning process. The effectiveness of the ASM methodology is confirmed through simulations with the MATLAB SerDes Toolbox, resulting in notable enhancements in the eye diagram area and overall system margins.

articleTitle: Frequency-domain ANN Non-linear Active Device Model for Harmonic-Balance-based CAD
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: In this work we demonstrate a feed-forward Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model for microwave active devices, here an FET, where the input and outputs are the device harmonic port waves. The ANN has been trained through an in-house tool implementing back-propagation and gradient descent, with load-pull data sweeping the available input power from back-off to harsh compression. The ANN model can be seamlessly used as a replacement of any active device model in microwave CAD tools implementing the Harmonic Balance (HB) algorithm. As a demonstrator, we developed in MATLAB an HB circuit solver implementing the ANN device model within an external circuit simulating the device with different loading conditions. The ANN modeling approach been successfully applied both in class A and a class B bias.

articleTitle: Modeling and Design of High Isolation Dual-Polarized Aperture-Coupled Microstrip Patch Antennas with Dual-Offset Feedlines
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: In this paper, the steps required to model and design high isolation dual-polarized aperture-coupled microstrip patch (ACMP) antennas with dual-offset feedlines are presented. The proposed approach requires that the effective impedance of the antenna when fed in a balanced mode be determined as a function of the distance between the dual-offset feedlines. Equations relating the effective impedance with the feed geometry are derived from experiments, enabling the design of matching networks for any given effective impedance. This study shows that ACMP antennas with dual-offset feedlines can be matched to the source using $\lambda / 4$ transformers and T -junctions. A 10 GHz dualpolarized antenna with dual-offset feedlines was designed and simulated in an electromagnetic solver using the proposed methodology. A return loss of 20.6 dB in port 1,51.1 dB return loss in port 2,75.5 dB of isolation between excitation ports, and crosspolarization levels below 60 dB at broadside were achieved.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Material Sensors based on Free-Running and Injection-Locked Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: We present novel topologies and analysis procedures for permittivity sensors based on oscillator circuits, operating in both free-running and injection-locked conditions. We analyze the sensing capabilities of oscillators using step-impedance resonators and slow-wave structures, influenced by the material under test (MUT). These structures are connected to the oscillator’s active core, modeled through a numerical nonlinear admittance function extracted from harmonic-balance (HB) simulations. The goal is to achieve high sensitivity with low phase-noise spectral density. When introducing an input signal, the locking band varies with the MUT. This band will be calculated with the aid of a nonlinear current function, obtained through HB. We introduce an innovative system driven by a chirped signal and an injection-locked dual-frequency sensor to enhance robustness. Very good agreement is obtained between simulations and measurements.

articleTitle: AI based Activity Monitoring in Washrooms using Low-Resolution Radar
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost radar monitoring system for comprehensive washroom activity analysis in elder care homes. Leveraging deep learning, this system can overcome the low resolution of inexpensive off-the-shelf radar to monitor residents with high accuracy. Radar data, in the form of Range-Elevation, Range-Doppler, and Range-Azimuth, is processed through a convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM) neural network architecture for activity classification and anomaly detection. Our methodology achieved an accuracy over 90% in identifying routine behaviours and fall events for 5 participants.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Load-Pull Extrapolation using Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Design optimization of high-power nonlinear power amplifiers requires much back-and-forth between power sweep, bias sweep, and load-pull simulations. Such manual optimizations are very slow given the large number of parameters and goals. The automation of this process holds promise for reducing time to successful designs in computer-aided design operations, especially in microwave power-amplifier design. This work proposes multidimensional image completion techniques using Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) as a method for reducing the number of simulation queries required to characterize a power amplifier over multiple design parameters simultaneously, such as input power and load impedance. Specifically, as few as 16 simulation queries are able to accurately predict the optimal reflection coefficient over input power to within a vector error of about 0.1, leading to significant time savings over other characterization methods.

articleTitle: Temperature-dependent electromagnetic characterisation of materials for CO2 capture and utilization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> capture and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> generation are part of global strategies to mitigate global warming. The use of microwaves for CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> capture and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> generation via DRM (Dry Reforming of Methane) is one of the most promising methods for utilizing green energy. To design CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> monolithic sorbents heated by microwaves, careful selection of materials is required to ensure they are chemically active for the expected reaction (DRM or CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> adsorption) and have suitable electromagnetic properties for efficient heating. This article demonstrates how the electromagnetic properties of various commercial and non-commercial materials have been measured for use in constructing monoliths for microwave power applicators.

articleTitle: Novel Method for Negative Group Delay Circuit with High Transmission Coefficient
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: As Negative Group Delay (NGD) circuits are based on filters, insertion loss (IL) is inherent to them with recent efforts to enhance the NGD per IL ratio. This work presents theory and simulation of a novel method to create NGD circuits without IL at the center frequency, this method is based on Negative Impedance Converter (NIC) integrated to the reactive elements, so the NGD behavior is rotated with relation to the horizontal axis. We use a series bandpass combined with the NIC to illustrate the technique. At the resonant frequency of 1GHz, the simulated result presents a NGD of -3.17 ns with no IL. The theoretical and simulated results are accurately matched.

articleTitle: A Multi-Platform GUI for Circuit Schematic Design Using CircuiTikZ
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: The powerful CircuiTikZ-package provides typesetting of electrical and electronic networks and is commonly used in all areas of electrical engineering. The TikZ-based syntax is powerful, but unintuitive and tedious, leading to a lot of time used for creating the schematic drawings. A browser-based graphical user interface (GUI) is presented that provides features such as “what you see is what you get” (WYSIWYG). The presented browser application lets the user design the circuitry graphically. The tool calculates the component positions based on user input and exports (Circui) TikZ code for use in LATEX like typesetting documents significantly speeding up the circuit schematic drawing process.

articleTitle: 2D Imaging of Graphene Oxide Electric Parameters with a 10 GHz Inverted Single-Post Dielectric Resonator
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Accurate measurement of conductivity and sheet resistance is essential for evaluating conductive materials, such as graphene oxide papers. This study employs a 10 GHz inverted Single-Post Dielectric Resonator (iSiPDR) integrated into a 2D scanning system to detect shifts in resonant frequency and Q - factor for thin films and bulk materials. The experimental setup, controlled by a Scanner Unit Control Application and a Vector Network Analyzer, enables the generation of 2D maps of material properties to identify variations and defects. Data analysis involves retro-modeling with a Body-of-Revolution Finite-Difference Time-Domain (BoR FDTD) algorithm and advanced signal processing techniques, including automated Prony methods, to accurately extract material parameters. This method provides a robust modelling-based characterization framework for material characterization, supporting quality control and optimization in microelectronics and battery technologies.

articleTitle: Comparison of Machine Learning Models for Spectral Binning Approach to Motion Classification in Doppler Radar Physiological Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: When using Doppler radar to monitor physiological motion such as that from cardiopulmonary activity, identification of the subject’s state of activity is essential in order to properly assess the measurement. This research examines the use of machine learning (ML) to classify a subject’s state of activity as sedentary, fidgeting, or ambulatory. It adopts a spectral binning approach which classifies components of the arctangent demodulated output signal from a quadrature 2.4-GHz CW Doppler radar system, based on spectral content associated with various frequency bins. Comparative performance was assessed for using Random Forest (RF) and Deep Neural Network (DNN) approaches varying in layers, neurons, and training batch sizes. The most accurate technique proved to be the RF method (93%). However, the other DNN methods also proved effective offering significant potential for robust automated assessment of a monitored subject’s state of activity.

articleTitle: GaN Technology as the Key to Efficient Solutions for High-Performance Class F Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Gallium Nitride (GaN) transistors have established themselves as a powerful alternative to Si-based Laterally-Diffused Metal-Oxide Semiconductor (LDMOS) transistors, particularly in high-frequency amplifiers. In this work, the use of GaN transistors in class F amplifiers at a frequency of 123.2 MHz and an output power of 100 W is investigated. The focus is on the optimization of the target impedances considering intrinsic and extrinsic parameters. A multiharmonics tuner was used to precisely adjust the impedances and contributed to the increase in performance. The results show that the amplifier achieves a maximum Power-Added Efficiency (PAE) of approximately 73.5 % with a compression of 3 dB. This work confirms the advantages of GaN transistors in high power applications and provides important insights for the further development of modern amplifier technologies in the VHF range.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Use of Asymmetric Feed in Planar Filters Based on Matryoshka Geometry
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Filters are essential devices in telecommunication systems, as they are responsible for selecting signals and, consequently, reducing possible interference that could damage the quality of the information. At GTEMA-IFPB, a geometry, called matryoshka has been used to make planar filters. Considering that, in order to obtain a certain frequency response, asymmetric feeding can be used as a design parameter, this work investigates this feeding. Parametric analysis is presented, describing how the different types of asymmetry influence the frequency response. Numerical and experimental results are presented for band-reject filters based on open square ring and matryoshka geometries, with rectangular rings, applied in the Wi-Fi range, specifically at 2.4 GHz. The results showed the miniaturization capacity and greater bandwidth for the asymmetric feed.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of the LPWAN Standards NB-IoT and LTE-M Based on Protocols and Message Volumes
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: The growing number of IoT devices necessitates sustainable hardware and software solutions. This work compares the power consumption of two low-power wireless communication boards, implementing the promising LPWAN standards NB-IoT and LTE-M with MQTT. The measurements assess the impact of the protocols on the overall energy efficiency. Subsequent research assessed the efficacy of data transmission strategies in the context of LPWAN systems, with a particular focus on the impact of message size and connection persistence on power efficiency. The findings indicated that strategic data aggregation and the maintenance of persistent connections enhance energy efficiency, guiding the development of more efficient IoT communication practices.

articleTitle: A Human Pose Recognition Model Comparison to Label Radar Data for Gesture Recognition in Robotics
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Instantaneous radar data labeling during data set acquisition, through camera based computer vision methods, is a challenging task. In context of human pose and gesture recognition, there is a huge amount of computer vision models available and whether they are suitable for instantaneous data labeling needs to be investigated. Therefore, this paper compares 20 different models regarding inference time and human keypoint location deviations. The most suitable model is statistically investigated further using more than 250 thousand images, where person presence detection and gesture detection are evaluated using simple threshold methods. Obtained results reveal 94% of all images are correctly classified.

articleTitle: Radon Transform Approaches in FMCW-Based-Sub-THz Tomography
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the use of two FMCW radars operating at a center frequency of 243.6 GHz to generate tomographic images of an object under test. The FMCW radar principle is used to measure the Radon projection. Unlike the standard Radon transform, this method allows the use of either attenuation or phase as the reconstruction quantity, with phase being particularly beneficial for low-permittivity materials. The tomographic image is reconstructed using the filtered back-projection method to solve the inverse Radon transform problem. To enhance the signal-to-noise ratio and improve wave focusing, two converging lenses are employed in the measurement setup.

articleTitle: A Wideband Low Power Single-to-Differential GaAs LNA for mmWave Spectrum Monitoring Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: The design of a low-power single-ended-to-differential low-noise amplifier (LNA) for spectrum monitoring applications is reported. The LNA is composed of a common source (CS) amplifier with inductive degeneration, followed by a common gate, common source (CGCS) active balun. The integrated 2 stage LNA have been designed at a central frequency of 25 GHz, with 10 GHz of bandwidth, using $\mathbf{0 . 1} \mu \mathrm{m}$ GaAs pseudomorphic high electron mobility transistors (pHEMT). The impact of the gate width and number of fingers on the performance is investigated. The simulations results show that the proposed 2 stage LNA achieves a 26 dB gain at 20 GHz and a noise figure of 0.86 dB, and remaining strong at 30 GHz with a gain of 21 dB and a noise figure of $\mathbf{1 . 2} \mathbf{~ d B}$. The power consumption of the LNA is 94 mW and has a compact chip size with an area of $1.5 \times 2.8 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Scanning Near-Field Microwave Microscopy of Sub-fF Vertical MOS Capacitors Using Six-Port Interferometry
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Scanning Microwave Microscopy (SMM) is a powerful technique for probing the electrical properties of nanoscale devices. In this work, we present a novel implementation of SMM considering a six-port interferometer as alternative to the conventional vector network analyzer (VNA). In particular, sub-fF vertical metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) microsized capacitors, are exemplary characterized using both proposed solution and conventional set-up. This approach extends the capabilities of six-port technology for accurate evaluation of highimpedance nanoscale devices, offering a more compact and costeffective solution for advanced SMM applications.

articleTitle: A 28 GHz Double Patch Double Beam Antenna with Circular Polarization for Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a double-patch, double-beam directional microstrip patch antenna, with circular polarization and enhanced bandwidth. The antenna design was accomplished by first creating a square patch resonating at the desired frequency. Subsequently, the ground plane was replaced by a second patch, identical to the initially designed one, resulting in a significant back lobe, nearly equivalent in size to the main lobe. Additionally, cuts were made at the corners of the patches to enhance antenna bandwidth and achieve circular polarization. This resulted in an antenna with an enhanced bandwidth of $\mathbf{1 . 6 9}$ $\mathbf{G H z}$ (27.17-28.86 GHz), covering the 28 GHz band (27.5-28.35 GHz). Moreover, it exhibits circular polarization within the frequency range of 27.88 GHz to 28.09 GHz, and a gain of 6.03 dBi for the principal lobe. The back one attains a comparable value. The antenna achieves an efficiency of $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$. The antenna size is $0.31 \lambda_{0} \times 0.31 \lambda_{0}$.

articleTitle: Combination of Geometries in SRR Structures for Optimizing Electromagnetic Wave Absorption in EMC Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This work investigates the electromagnetic absorption efficiency of metamaterials using split-ring resonators (SRR) in combined geometries, specifically integrating circular and square SRRs. Through numerical algorithm, the dimensional parameters were optimized to maximize absorption at specific frequencies. The analyses showed that the combined structures maintain high absorption efficiency, especially at frequencies of $2.5 \mathrm{GHz}, 3.1 \mathrm{GHz}$, and 3.8 GHz, with variations in incidence angles of $30^{\circ} \mathbf{4 5}^{\circ}$, and 60°. Absorption at 3.1 GHz reached up to $\mathbf{9 9 \%}$, suggesting an ideal configuration for higher angles. The results highlight the importance of considering the incidence angle in the design of metamaterials, reinforcing the potential of these materials in practical applications, such as radar systems and electromagnetic protection.

articleTitle: Cardiff Behavioral Model Analysis for Frequency Doubler Design
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: The Cardiff behavioral model is a robust nonlinear tool for guiding nonlinear circuit design. This paper proposes a methodology to generate Cardiff AB models suitable for microwave frequency doubler optimization. Active Load-Pull data from both measurement and simulations are processed through a self-developed MATLAB application to extract and evaluate Cardiff AB models formulated with different mixing orders and number of parameters. Moreover, the role of harmonic source and load impedances in model extraction for frequency doubler design space prediction is studied.

articleTitle: Heart Rate Variability Sensing Using Channel State Information of Millimeter-Wave OFDM Communication Signals
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Unobtrusive physiological sensing is a promising tool for example for sleep monitoring, elderly care, and automotive in-cabin monitoring. Doppler radar physiological sensing can provide respiratory and cardiovascular parameters without physical contact, both with dedicated hardware and by using channel measurement that provides channel state information (CSI) in communication systems. To the best of the author’s knowledge, this paper presents the first heart rate variability (HRV) measurement using a millimeter-wave OFDM communication system. Template matching and wavelet transform techniques that were previously developed for obtaining HRV parameters with a stand-alone Doppler radar system were applied to CSI amplitude and phase. HRV parameters were obtained with accuracy within 10ms compared to PPG reference for three human subjects. In addition, the benefits of using different communication channels to take advantage of frequency diversity were illustrated for both CSI amplitude and phase data.

articleTitle: A 148-166 GHz Meissner Push-Push VCO With -168 dBc/Hz FOMT Using a Single Transformer in SiGe BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents a fully integrated push-push voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) using a modified Meissner (Armstrong) topology based on a single asymmetric transformer and varactor, which achieves a frequency tuning range (FTR) of $11.6 \%$ between 148.4 GHz and 166.7 GHz at a maximum output power of -1.7dBm. The target application is the generation of flexible local oscillator (LO) signals for Joint Communication and Sensing (JCAS) applications in the D-band. A minimum phase noise of -80.6 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset is achieved at a power consumption of 54 mW from a 1.8 V supply, which corresponds to a $\mathrm{FOM}_{\mathrm{T}}$ of $-168.5 \mathrm{dBc} / \mathrm{Hz}$. The VCO test structure is fabricated using a $130 \mathrm{~nm} \operatorname{SiGe} \mathrm{BiCMOS}$ technology with $f_{\mathrm{t}} / f_{\text {max }}$ of $250 \mathrm{GHz} / 370 \mathrm{GHz}$ and is co-integrated with a static divide-by-32 frequency divider chain that provides an output at around 2.5 GHz for interfacing with an external phase-locked loop (PLL).

articleTitle: Modified Koch Fractal Antenna for IoT Applications in Smart Homes
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a microstrip antenna for IoT (Internet of Things) applications in Smart Homes, incorporating fractal geometry and a defected ground structure (DGS) to enhance the antenna’s bandwidth and gain, respectively. The proposed design is based on the Koch fractal and a cross-shaped slot for the DGS. The operating frequency is 5.8 GHz. The antenna was simulated using Ansys HFSS, and experimentally validated with measurements of a manufactured prototype on a PCB substrate. Results show a bandwidth of 127.30 MHz, return loss of -39.12 dB, gain of 12.85 dBi, efficiency of 0.78, and directivity of 16.44 dBi.

articleTitle: Microwave Photonics Computational Signal Algebra Framework for Radar Integrated Sensing and Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This work presents a computational signal algebra (CSA) framework for microwave photonics signal processing efforts in radar integrated sensing and communication (RISC) applications, for areas such as parameter estimation, beamforming, and waveform design. The proposed framework presents a set of computational methods, with an associated visualization environment for time-frequency tools such as the short-time Fourier transform (STFT), the cross-ambiguity function (CAF), and the Wigner-Ville distribution (WVD). The discrete ambiguity function (DAF) was implemented as a user defined function (UDF) to be used as a signal correlation analysis and waveform design tool aiming at assisting in research efforts towards efficient use of the electromagnetic spectrum by reducing noise and interference and adhering to spectrum management regulatory standards. Significant computational speedups were obtained for the CAF by introducing novel data sampling algorithmic techniques. Finally, an information flow security framework is proposed utilizing a post-quantum cryptography (PQC) approach in RISC environments.

articleTitle: TCAD accurate modeling of trap-induced effects in GaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: In this work we demonstrate an accurate Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) modeling approach for the analysis of trap effects on the electrical features of AlGaN/GaN HEMT devices for microwave applications. The physical device model includes the discretized coupled drift-diffusion and trap rate equations system, implemented into an in-house mixed-mode TCAD simulator, and solved in dynamic conditions with the Harmonic Balance (HB) algorithm. The TCAD allows a seamless assessment of the DC, small-signal AC and periodic large-signal (LS) behavior of GaN HEMTs as a function of the trap properties. A test-case addresses the analysis of 29 GHz class B power amplifier based on a Fe-doped 150 nm GaN HEMT as a function of the Fe trap energy, showing that, despite a marked signature on the AC parameters dispersion, traps have a mild impact on single-tone LS behavior even in strongly non-linear operation.

articleTitle: Efficient Design of Compact and Wideband Microstrip Filters Using Space Mapping and Surrogate-Based Modeling Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This article describes a systematic design approach, based on the use of surrogate models in a low-accuracy space, to achieve smaller footprints and wider bandwidths for direct-coupled microstrip filter topologies. To reduce the computational cost of the design procedure, the frequency response of each resonant structure is matched (individually) to that of its equivalent circuit model, thus avoiding extensive optimization at electromagnetic (EM) level. The designed filter can then be translated into a high-accuracy space using the Aggressive Space Mapping (ASM) technique. In addition, an equivalent circuit based on a combination of inductive, capacitive and distributed elements is firstly synthesized. Results for the new filter topology are fully validated, through full-wave EM simulations from two commercial codes, and successfully compared (in terms of size and performance) with those of traditional coupled-line filters.

articleTitle: Towards Spectrum Sensing Within 6th Generation Mobile Communications in the Sub-6 GHz Frequency Range Using Wideband Direct Sampling Architectures
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Within this work, a pre-processing system for spectrum sensing is demonstrated. A full hardware-software codesign implementation is demonstrated. Spectral analysis patterns are generated, various transmission properties are evaluated. Furthermore, signal degradation effects caused by ADC and DAC artifacts are discussed. Even within a a loopback system from DAC to ADC a power spectral density difference of 2.2 dB can be observed within the usable transmission band, with even higher disruptions around the Nyquist limits. Ultimately, mitigation strategies for these signal impairments are discussed.

articleTitle: An X-Band Frequency Selective Rasorber Based on Concentric Split Ring Slots
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency selective rasorber (FSR) with absorption-transmission-absorption (A-T-A) capabilities at X-band. The proposed FSR consists of a dual-layer array, where the unit cell of the first layer contains three concentric split ring slots with resonant frequencies located within the X band. The inner and the outer rings are loaded with lumped resistors to increase the absorptivity at the lower and upper bands, while the middle ring is not loaded to allow a passband for the center frequencies. The second layer contains miniaturized ring slots to provide high transmission to the center passband. Due to the proximity between frequencies, the resonance’s selectivity of the second layer needs to be high; therefore, a unit cell with four small ring slots loaded by capacitors is used. Simulated results show that this FSR demonstrates absorption peaks of $87.4 \%$ and $94.4 \%$ at the lower and upper absorptive bands, respectively, and insertion loss lower than 2 dB is obtained at the transmissive band from 9.59 to 9.86 GHz. One can conclude that this design can reach very high absorption rates without increasing insertion loss at the transmission window.

articleTitle: Cognitive Parameter Extraction for Space Mapping Design Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Parameter extraction (PE) is a key subproblem of space mapping (SM) design optimization. It consists of a local alignment between the coarse and fine models at each SM iteration. In this work, cognition-driven PE is proposed for SM. In contrast to classical PE, where the full fine model responses are used as targets, the proposed cognitive PE focuses on key features of the fine model response selected from an engineering perspective. It is demonstrated that the proposed cognitive PE approach: 1) yields more accurate extracted parameters regardless of the type of PE objective function employed; and 2) achieves a more meaningful matching to the fine model target response and with less variability. To proof this with independence of the optimization method employed for PE, plots of the PE objective functions are presented over large regions of the coarse model design space. Two synthetic examples are used to support these findings.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Full Mixed-Mode Performance of a Differential Microstrip Interconnect with a Right-Angle Bend by using Two Symmetrical Bumps
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Differential interconnects are widely used for high-speed serial data transmission in modern high-performance computer platforms. Differential signaling handle noise better than single ended signaling. However, physical asymmetries and discontinuities in differential links can cause that a portion of the differential energy is converted into common mode (CM) energy, which is perceived as noise at the receiver. This mode conversion in differential interconnects leads to electromagnetic (EM) interference and EM susceptibility, limiting high data rates. In this paper, a microstrip differential interconnect with a severe discontinuity, a right-angle bend, is optimally compensated by using two rectangular length-match bumps. Our formulation allows the efficient optimization of the full set of mixed-mode (MM) S-parameters of the differential interconnect. It uses a smart combination of pattern search and Nelder-Mead to optimize the MM performance considering several starting points. The interconnect MM performance before and after optimization is shown, confirming a very significant performance improvement.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Reflectarray Antenna on FR4 Substrate for Dual Linear Polarization at 100 GHz
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a wideband reflectarray antenna supporting dual polarization in simulation. The unit cell comprises two orthogonal sets of three coplanar parallel dipoles printed on two surfaces. The lengths of the coupled dipoles are optimized and varied to achieve a phase range exceeding 360 degrees for both orthogonal linear polarizations. Simulation results show peak gains of 32.9 dBi for x-polarization and 30.84 dBi for y-polarization at 100 GHz. The antenna also exhibits a 3 dB gain bandwidth of 17% for x-polarization (93 GHz to 110 GHz) and 25% for y-polarization (93 GHz to 118 GHz), with low cross-polarization levels.

articleTitle: Analysis of Additive Manufacturing Polymer Technologies and Metallization Techniques for the Development of Microwave Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents an approach for manufacturing high-performance microwave communication devices using additive manufacturing (AM) focusing on metal alloys and metallized polymers. We detail the design, fabrication, and characterization of the devices. Comprehensive analyses of manufacturing tolerances, assembling gaps, and material properties alights the relationship between fabrication processes and device performance, demonstrating that AM can develop lightweight, highly integrated microwave components with superior performance and reduced manufacturing costs.

articleTitle: A Broadband Sub-THz Push-Push Frequency Doubler in 22 nm FDSOI
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents a sub-THz push-push frequency doubler with a D-band power amplifier (PA) chain demonstrated in a 22 nm fully-depleted silicon-on-insulator (FDSOI) technology. The D-band PA comprises three common-source (CS) driver stages and a high-power stacked output stage. The amplifier stages utilize the capacitive neutralization technique for gain-boosting. Two parallel push-push doubler stages are employed after the PA. The input power distribution and matching to the PA optimum load-pull point are achieved by leveraging an area-efficient stacked transformer with two secondary coils. The overall circuitry occupies a compact core area of $0.0625 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$. The PA and frequency doubler attains a maximal gain of 7 dB and a saturated output power $P_{\text {sat }}$ of -5 dBm, covering a 60 GHz 3 dB -bandwidth. Furthermore, the circuits exhibits a minimum suppression of 35 dBc to the fundamental frequency. The circuit’s DC-power consumption is below 230 mW, supplied by 1.6 V and 0.8 V.

articleTitle: A J- and D-Band Dual-Band Receiver for FMCW Radar and RadCom in a SiGe Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents a compact dual-band receiver for radar and RadCom applications, capable of simultaneously down-converting J -band $(220-325 \mathrm{GHz})$ and D-band ($110-170 \mathrm{GHz}$) signals with high conversion gain. Implemented in 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology, the receiver uses two stacked switching quads to subharmonically mix the J-band RF signal and down-convert D-band signals without additional circuit components. The in-phase LO signal driving both switching quads eliminates the need for 90° couplers, reducing the overall area to $(235 \times 180) \mu \mathrm{m}^{2}$. The receiver achieves peak conversion gains of 15 dB at 324 GHz and 19.7 dB at 162 GHz, with DSB noise figures below 21.9 dB and 15.9 dB, respectively, at a total power consumption of 129 mW. This low area and power consumption make large MIMO arrays with closely spaced dual-band antennas feasible for future RadCom applications.
